verses.zh: 弟兄们，我还有话说：我们靠着主耶稣求你们，劝你们，你们既然受了我们的教训，知道该怎样行可以讨　神的喜悦，就要照你们现在所行的更加勉励。
verses.en: Finally then, brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] we ask you and urge you in the Lord Jesus, that as you received instruction from us about how[NOTE:2] you must live and please God (as you are in fact living)[NOTE:3] that you do so more and more.
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:4.

As you received instruction from us about how (Grk “as you received from us how”). The Greek word translated received is used for accepting instructions passed on as fixed traditions from teacher to follower. Paul speaks in these terms about doctrinal traditions as well as ethical instruction that he passes on to his converts and expects them to keep (cf. 1 Cor 11:2, 23; 15:1-3; Gal 1:9; Phil 4:9; 2 Thess 2:15; 3:6).

This parenthetical clause is absent in several later witnesses (D2 Ψ 1175 1241 2464vid M al), but it may have been expunged for sounding redundant. The longer text, in this instance, is solidly supported by א A B D* F G 0183vid 0278 33 81 104 326 365 629 al co and should be unquestionably preferred.

verses.zh: 你们原晓得，我们凭主耶稣传给你们甚么命令。
verses.en: For you know what commands we gave you through the Lord Jesus.

verses.zh: 神的旨意就是要你们成为圣洁，远避淫行；
verses.en: For this is God’s will: that you become holy,[NOTE:1] that you keep away from sexual immorality,
notes: Or “your sanctification.”

verses.zh: 要你们各人晓得怎样用圣洁、尊贵守着自己的身体，
verses.en: that each of you know how to possess his own body[NOTE:1] in holiness and honor,
notes: Grk “to gain [or possess] his own vessel.” “Vessel” is most likely used figuratively for “body” (cf. 2 Cor 4:7). Some take it to mean “wife” (thus, “to take a wife for himself” or “to live with his wife”), but this is less likely. See J. Smith, “1 Thess 4:4—Breaking the Impasse,” BBR 10 (Fall 2000), who argues that “vessel” in this context is very likely a euphemism for the sexual organs.

verses.zh: 不放纵私欲的邪情，像那不认识　神的外邦人。
verses.en: not in lustful passion like the Gentiles who do not know God.

verses.zh: 不要一个人在这事上越分，欺负他的弟兄；因为这一类的事，主必报应，正如我预先对你们说过、又切切嘱咐你们的。
verses.en: In this matter no one should violate the rights of his brother or take advantage of him,[NOTE:1] because the Lord is the avenger in all these cases,[NOTE:2] as we also told you earlier and warned you solemnly.
notes: Grk “not to transgress against or defraud his brother in the matter,” continuing the sentence of vv. 3-5.
Grk “concerning all these things.”

verses.zh: 神召我们，本不是要我们沾染污秽，乃是要我们成为圣洁。
verses.en: For God did not call us to impurity but in holiness.

verses.zh: 所以，那弃绝的，不是弃绝人，乃是弃绝那赐圣灵给你们的　神。
verses.en: Consequently the one who rejects this is not rejecting human authority[NOTE:1] but God, who gives his Holy Spirit to you.
notes: Grk “rejecting man.”

verses.zh: 论到弟兄们相爱，不用人写信给你们；因为你们自己蒙了　神的教训，叫你们彼此相爱。
verses.en: Now on the topic of brotherly love[NOTE:1] you have no need for anyone to write you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another.
notes: Grk “concerning brotherly love.”

verses.zh: 你们向马其顿全地的众弟兄固然是这样行，但我劝弟兄们要更加勉励。
verses.en: And indeed you are practicing it toward all the brothers and sisters[NOTE:1] in all of Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers and sisters, to do so more and more,[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “brothers”; this applies to the second occurrence as well. See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:4.
To do so more and more. See a similar phrase in 1 Thess 4:1.

verses.zh: 又要立志作安静人，办自己的事，亲手做工，正如我们从前所吩咐你们的，
verses.en: to aspire to lead a quiet life, to attend to your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you.

verses.zh: 叫你们可以向外人行事端正，自己也就没有甚么缺乏了。
verses.en: In this way you will live[NOTE:1] a decent life before outsiders and not be in need.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “that you may live,” continuing the sentence of 4:10b-11.
Or “not be dependent on anyone”; Grk “and have need of nothing,” “of no one.”

verses.zh: 论到睡了的人，我们不愿意弟兄们不知道，恐怕你们忧伤，像那些没有指望的人一样。
verses.en: Now we do not want you to be uninformed,[NOTE:1] brothers and sisters,[NOTE:2] about those who are asleep,[NOTE:3] so that you will not grieve like the rest who have no hope.
notes: Grk “ignorant.”
Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:4.

Most witnesses have the perfect participle κεκοιμημένων here (“who have fallen asleep” [D (F G) Ψ 1241 1505 1881 2464 M al]), but the present participle κοιμωμένων (“who are asleep”) is better supported by early and significant mss (א A B 0278 33 81 1175 1739 al) and should be considered the Ausgangstext. tn The verb κοιμάω (koimaō) literally means “sleep,” but it is often used in the Bible as a euphemism for death when speaking of believers. This metaphorical usage by its very nature emphasizes the hope of resurrection: Believers will one day “wake up” out of death. Here the term refers to death, but “sleep” was used in the translation to emphasize the metaphorical, rhetorical usage of the term. This word also occurs in vv. 14 and 15.

verses.zh: 我们若信耶稣死而复活了，那已经在耶稣里睡了的人，　神也必将他们与耶稣一同带来。
verses.en: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also we believe that[NOTE:1] God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep as Christians.[NOTE:2]
notes: “we believe that” is understood from the first clause of the verse, which is parallel. Grk “so also God will bring.”

Grk “those who have fallen asleep through Jesus.” It is possible that “through Jesus” describes “bring,” but this gives the unlikely double reference, “through Jesus God will bring them with Jesus.” Instead it describes their “falling sleep,” since through him their death is only sleep and not the threat it once was. Also Christians are those whose total existence—life and death—is in and through and for Christ (1 Cor 8:6).

verses.zh: 我们现在照主的话告诉你们一件事：我们这活着还存留到主降临的人，断不能在那已经睡了的人之先。
verses.en: For we tell you this by the word of the Lord,[NOTE:1] that we who are alive, who are left until the coming of the Lord, will surely not go ahead of those who have fallen asleep.
notes: The word of the Lord is a technical expression in OT literature, often referring to a divine prophetic utterance (e.g., Gen 15:1, Isa 1:10, Jonah 1:1). In the NT it occurs 15 times: 3 times as ῥῆμα τοῦ κυρίου (rhēma tou kuriou; Luke 22:61, Acts 11:16, 1 Pet 1:25) and 12 times as λόγος τοῦ κυρίου (logos tou kuriou; here and in Acts 8:25; 13:44, 48, 49; 15:35, 36; 16:32; 19:10, 20; 1 Thess 1:8; 2 Thess 3:1). As in the OT, this phrase focuses on the prophetic nature and divine origin of what has been said.

verses.zh: 因为主必亲自从天降临，有呼叫的声音和天使长的声音，又有　神的号吹响；那在基督里死了的人必先复活。
verses.en: For the Lord himself will come down from heaven with a shout of command, with the voice of the archangel,[NOTE:1] and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first.
notes: Neither noun in this phrase (ἐν φωνῇ ἀρχαγγέλου, en phōnē archangelou, “with the voice of the archangel”) has the article in keeping with Apollonius’ Canon. Since ἀρχάγγελος (archangelos) is most likely par excellence, both nouns are translated as definite in keeping with Apollonius’ Corollary (see ExSyn 250-51).

verses.zh: 以后我们这活着还存留的人必和他们一同被提到云里，在空中与主相遇。这样，我们就要和主永远同在。
verses.en: Then we who are alive, who are left,[NOTE:1] will be suddenly caught up[NOTE:2] together[NOTE:3] with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so we will always be with the Lord.
notes: The words οἱ περιλειπόμενοι (hoi perileipomenoi, “[the ones] who are left”) are lacking in F G 0226vid ar b as well as a few fathers, but the rest of the textual tradition has the words. Most likely, the Western mss omitted the words because of perceived redundancy with οἱ ζῶντες (hoi zōntes, “[the ones] who are alive”).
Or “snatched up.” The Greek verb ἁρπάζω implies that the action is quick or forceful, so the translation supplied the adverb “suddenly” to make this implicit notion clear.
Or “simultaneously,” but this meaning does not fit as well in the parallel in 5:10.

verses.zh: 所以，你们当用这些话彼此劝慰。
verses.en: Therefore encourage one another with these words.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

EXPANDED OUTLINE OF 1 Thessalonians 4:1-12

- Introductory remarks, 1 Thess. 4:1-2

- Warnings about sexual immorality, 1 Thess. 4:3-8. For more information see the list of the inappropriate
actions and motives of Paul's opponents at 1 Thess. 1:5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 1 THESSALONIANS 4:1-8

1Finally, then, brethren, we request and exhort you in the Lord Jesus, that
as you received from us instruction as to how you ought to walk and please God (just as you actually do walk), that you excel still more.
2For you know what commandments we gave you by the authority of the Lord Jesus. 3For this is the will of
God, your sanctification; that is, that you abstain from sexual immorality; 4that each of you know how to possess his own
vessel in sanctification and honor, 5not in lustful passion, like the Gentiles who do not know God; 6and that
no man transgress and defraud his brother in the matter because the Lord is the avenger in all these things, just as we also told you before
and solemnly warned you. 7For God has not called us for the purpose of impurity, but in sanctification. 8So, he
who rejects this is not rejecting man but the God who gives His Holy Spirit to you.

4:1 "Finally then" This is literally "for the rest." This possibly begins Paul's practical section. Most
of Paul's letters can be divided into a doctrinal section and a practical section although it is hard
to do this in 1 Thessalonians. Paul often used this phrase to introduce the last major subject, not as an
immediate prelude to a closing (e.g. 2 Cor. 13:11; Eph. 6:10; 2 Thess. 3:1).

▣ "brethren" Paul often uses this term (cf. 1 Thess. 1:4; 2:1,9,14,17; 3:7; 4:1,10,13; 5:1,4,12,
14,25,26,27; 2 Thess. 1:3; 2:1,13,15; 3:1,6,13). This is obviously a generic reference to all believers.

- to start a new subject

- to endear himself to his readers/listeners

▣ "request and exhort" Paul uses these PRESENT ACTIVE INDICATIVES to
emphasize continuing action and to soften his commands as an Apostle (cf. 1 Thess. 4:2,11;
2 Thess. 3:4,6,10,12).

▣ "as you received from us instruction" This is an AORIST ACTIVE INDICATIVE,
which points to the time Paul was with them personally. This is the Greek term that means "receive
traditional teachings from another" (cf. 1 Thess. 2:13; 2 Thess. 2:15; 3:6; 1 Cor. 11:2,23; 15:1; Gal. 1:9;
Phil. 4:9). Paul not only taught them how to be saved (justification), but also how to live as saved people (sanctification).
Justification must never be separated from sanctification! Never!

▣ "as to how you ought to walk" This is a PRESENT INFINITIVE. Walk is
biblical imagery for daily lifestyle faith (cf. 1 Thess. 2:12; Eph. 2:10; 4:1,17; 5:2,15; Col. 1:10; 2:6).
Christianity was originally called "The Way" (cf. Acts 9:2; 19:9,23; 22:4; 24:14,22; 18:25-26). This
speaks of an abiding lifestyle faith. Our initial response in repentance and faith must be followed
by continuing repentance, faith, obedience, and perseverance. Eternal life has observable characteristics!
In Christ every day is sacred, special, and used for worship and ministry.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "and please God" God's will for His children is not heaven when they die only, but
Christlikeness now (cf. Rom. 8:28-29; 2 Cor. 3:18; 7:1; Gal. 4:19; Eph. 1:4; 2:10; 4:13; 1 Thess. 3:13;
4:7; 5:23; 1 Pet. 1:15). God wants a people who reflect His character to a lost and needy world!

NASB
"(just as you actually do walk)"

NKJV
—omitted—

NRSV
"(as, in fact, you are doing)"

TEV
"This is, of course, the way you have been living"

NJB
"as you are already living it"

REB
"you are indeed already following it"

A Greek manuscript problem is connected to this phrase. This phrase is missing in the
Greek uncial manuscripts Dc, K, L, and the Textus Receptus texts. It is present in
MSS א, A, B, D*, F, G and also in the Syriac, Coptic,
and Vulgate translations. It is surprising that the early manuscripts have it and the later ones
omit it. This implies that it was dropped out accidently. The UBS4 rates its inclusion
as "A" (certain).

This is either PRESENT INDICATIVE or IMPERATIVE MOOD. It
is probably INDICATIVE in that it asserts Paul's confidence in their Christlike
lifestyle (cf. NASB, NRSV, TEV, and JB).

▣ "that you excel still more" They were doing well, but Paul urged them on to even
greater holiness (cf. 1 Thess. 4:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOUND (perisseuō)

4:2

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"commandments"

NRSV, NJB, TEV

"instructions"

REB

"rules"

This is a rare military word for authoritative commands handed down through the ranks
(cf. 1 Tim. 1:5, 18). I have included my Special Topic on the use of this word in John that parallels Paul's usage.
The New Covenant does have requirements (i.e. Matt. 11:29, rabbinical use of "yoke"). I would denote the
requirements of Jesus as

- need to repent (initially and continuously; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [NT])

- need for faith (initially and continuously; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST)

- obedience (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- service

- love for the Triune God and His people (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVE)

- worship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

- Christlikeness (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NT EVIDENCE OF ONE'S SALVATION)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "COMMANDMENT" IN JOHN'S WRITINGS

▣ "by the authority of the Lord Jesus" These were not Paul's personal thoughts but
Jesus' teachings. Paul's Apostolic authority rested on Jesus' authority (cf. 1 Thess. 4:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

4:3-6 This is one sentence in Greek.

4:3 "For this is the will of God" There is no ARTICLE, therefore, this is one of
God's wills (cf. Eph. 5:17), after salvation (cf. John 6:40).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WILL
(thelēma) OF GOD

▣ "your sanctification" This word shares the same root word with "holy" and "saints."
Sanctification, like justification, is an initial instantaneous act of grace (cf. 1 Cor. 1:2,30; 6:11).
Positionally, believers are in Christ. However, it should develop into lifestyle character, progressive
sanctification (cf. 1 Thess. 4:7; 3:13; Rom. 6:19-23). God's will for every Christian is Christlikeness!!
We cannot separate justification from sanctification!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

▣ "abstain from sexual immorality" This is literally "fornication." Premarital and extramarital
sex were distinguished in the OT by separate words, but this word's meaning was broader in scope in the NT.
"Fornication" meant all inappropriate sexual activity, including homosexuality and bestiality. Often
pagan worship included sexual activity (i.e. imitation magic, cf. 1 Thess. 5:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOMOSEXUALITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: ADULTERY

4:4

"to possess"

NRSV
"to control"

TEV

NJB

Peshitta
"to keep"

This is a PRESENT MIDDLE (deponent) INFINITIVE. It is
literally "to continually acquire" or "to possess."

NASB, NKJV
"his own vessel"

NRSV
"your own body"

TEV
"a wife"

NJB
"the body that belongs to him"

Peshitta

This can refer to "his own body" or "his own wife." Theodore of Mopsuestia, Augustine,
rabbinical usage, 1 Pet. 3:7, and the Septuagint interpret this in the sense of "wife" (cf. TEV). But
the early Church Fathers (i.e. Tertullian and Chrysostom) interpreted it as "body" and this fits the
context best (cf. NRSV, JB, NIV). Vessel is used in the sense of "body" in 2 Cor. 4:7.

▣ "in sanctification and honor" Knowing Jesus changes the way one lives. Believers are stewards,
dependent on another's will. God's will is to use every believer to show His transforming power to a
lost world. Christian marriage is a powerful witness in a fallen confused world!

4:5 "not in lustful passion" This refers to fallen mankind's inability to control themselves
sexually (pagan worship). Sexuality is a gift of God (cf. Genesis 1-2), but like all of God's gifts, they are taken
beyond God-given bounds by fallen humans.

Self-control is a characteristic of a Spirit filled, Spirit led life (cf. Gal. 5:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

▣ "like the Gentiles" This is literally "the nations." The lifestyle of the pagans of Paul's day was very immoral.

▣ "who do not know God" This does not exclude "natural revelation" (cf. Ps. 19:1-6 and
Romans 1-2), but speaks of personal knowledge (cf. Gal. 4:8-9). In the OT "know" can have the connotation
of intimate, personal relationship (cf. Gen.4:1; Jer. 1:5). Gentiles are estranged from God
(cf. Eph. 2:11-13; 5:8; Col. 1:21), but tragically, so are the Jews.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

4:6 "transgress" This term means "to go beyond bounds."

▣ "defraud" This term means "to take advantage of." It is related to the term "greed."

▣ "his brother" This may relate to taking sexual liberties with another believer's family
(cf. 1 Thess. 4:9). But the term "brother" in context could refer to any other human, similar to "neighbor"
(cf. 1 Thess. 4:12).

False teachers are often characterized by

- sexual exploitation

- financial exploitation

- claims of special privilege and special revelations

▣ "in the matter" This has the DEFINITE ARTICLE and therefore refers to
1 Thess. 4:3-5 (i.e. sexual purity). The word itself refers to business affairs. Therefore, it could
be used as imagery for

- sexual matters

- or Paul changes subjects in 1 Thess. 4:6 and is now dealing with financial issues

- I think the first option is best.

▣ "because the Lord is the avenger in all these things" This refers to even-handed
justice—both temporal (cf. Rom. 1:24,26,28) and eschatological (cf. Matt. 25:31ff.). YHWH is an
ethical God (cf. Gal. 6:7.) In 1 Thess. 4:6, 7a and 8a, three different reasons are given why the
believers should live holy lives.

▣ "as we also told you before and solemnly warned you" This is a strong statement
concerning sexual purity (cf. Heb. 13:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S USE OF HUPER COMPOUNDS

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

4:7 "God. . .called" God always takes the initiative (cf. John 6:44,65) both in salvation (justification) and in
the Christian life (sanctification).

This truth of the initiating sovereignty of our Creator God does not diminish His requirements of
fallen mankind's repentant, faith response. Mankind's relationship with God is characterized by a turning "from"
(repentance) and a turning "to" (faith). God has chosen to deal with fallen mankind by means of covenant. A good
example of the dual aspect can be illustrated from Phil. 2:12-13!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "sanctification" See note at v. 3.

4:8 "he who rejects this is not rejecting man but the God" This is literally "treat as of
little value." Paul asserts that along with the truth of the gospel goes the lifestyle imperatives.
These are God's truths, not Paul's, 1 Thess. 2:13; 3:1-2. Godly lives do not commend us to God, but that is the only
path after meeting Him in Christ (i.e. Eph. 2:8-9,10).

▣ "who gives His Holy Spirit to you" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE. There
was a major fight in the early church over who sent the Spirit.

- the Father

- the Son

- both

This refers to the indwelling Spirit as both an initial and ongoing experience (i.e. Acts 2:38; 2 Cor. 1:22;
5:5; 1 John 3:24).

All three persons of the Trinity are involved in all the redemptive events. Believers are indwelt by

- the Spirit (cf. Rom. 8:9-10)

- the Son (cf. Matt. 28:20; Col. 1:27)

- the Father (cf. John 14:23)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT (gift of. . .)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 1 THESSALONIANS 4:9-12

9Now as to the love of the brethren, you have no need for anyone to write to you,
for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another; 10for indeed you do practice it toward all the brethren who are in all Macedonia.
But we urge you, brethren, to excel still more, 11and to make it your ambition to lead a quiet life and attend to your own business and work
with your hands, just as we commanded you, 12so that you will behave properly toward outsiders and not be in any need.

4:9

NASB
"love of the brethren"

NKJV, Peshitta
"brotherly love"

NRSV
"love of the brothers and sisters"

TEV
"love for your fellow believers"

NJB
"loving our brothers"

This is the Greek term, philadelphia. This refers to love for covenant
partners (cf. Rom. 12:10; Heb. 13:1; 1 Pet. 1:23; 2 Pet. 1:7). The balancing statement about loving
the lost is in 1 Thess. 4:12 (cf. 1 Thess. 3:12).

▣ "you have no need for anyone to write to you" This was Paul's tactful way of affirming
them and yet encouraging them to greater effort (cf. 1 Thess. 4:10c). This does not refer to doctrinal
matters (i.e. the Second Coming), but practical, ethical lifestyle.

This may reflect the New Covenant of Jer. 31:31-34.

▣ "for you yourselves are taught by God" This is PRESENT TENSE. The teaching
continues as the indwelling Spirit continues (cf. 1 Thess. 5:1; John 14:26; 16:13; 2 Cor. 9:1;
1 John 2:20,27), which is a sign of the New Covenant (cf. Jer. 31:33-34).

The Greek term theodidaktoi (found only here in the NT) means "God taught" (cf. John 6:45)
and its object is to "love one another" (cf. John 13:34; 15:12,17; 1 John 2:7-8; 3:11,23; 2 John 5). Love is the uncounterfeitable
characteristic of YHWH (cf. 1 John 4:7-21)!

4:10 "you do practice" This is another PRESENT TENSE VERB which speaks of continuing
action (cf. 1 Thess. 4:17). Paul affirms their love but challenges them to do even more (as he did
their lifestyle purity in 1 Thess. 4:1).

▣ "to excel still more" They are doing a good job, but need to keep on even more
(cf. 1 Thess. 4:1). Love is the unique signature of God (cf. 1 Corinthians 13). We never love enough (cf. 1 Thess. 3:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOUND

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVE (agapē)

4:11

NASB

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS TO 4:13-5:11

The context about the Second coming runs through 1 Thess. 5:11. Remember its focus is pastoral
(cf. 1 Cor. 15:58). Doctrine is given, but only as it serves a godly lifestyle now!

I am amazed how many other eschatological events (usually from Daniel 9; 11) are assumed
in this context (same is true of 1 Corinthians 15, esp. v. 58). Believers must be very careful of combining inspired texts
in such a way as to give divine authority to human end-time schemes, systems, charts, and timelines.

In the area of eschatology, dogmatism and judgmentalism are always inappropriate. The church, from
its very beginning, has not agreed on how to interpret or systematize the end-time events, people, nor a schedule/timeline!

Three small books from Zondervan that have helped me in this area of theology are:

- Four Views of the Book of Revelation (1998)

- Three Views on the Rapture (2010)

- Three Views on the Millennium (1999)

They allow each view to present itself and then the other view gets to show its weaknesses.

Another book that has been so helpful in interpreting prophecy and apocalyptic is D. Brent Sandy,
Plowshares and Pruning Hooks.

4:13 "we do not want you to be uninformed, brethren" This is a common phrase in Paul's writings
(cf. Rom. 1:13; 11:25; 1 Cor. 10:1; 12:1; 2 Cor. 1:8). Usually it introduced an important statement,
similar to Jesus' use of "Amen, amen." Knowledge of Christian truth (doctrine and worldview) gives
believers a stability in a fallen world. Thank God for a written revelation!

Paul uses several similar expressions to introduce important statements or truths.

- "I wish you to know that. . ." ‒ 1 Cor. 11:3; Col. 2:1

- "I make known to you brothers" ‒ 1 Cor. 15:1; 2 Cor. 8:1; Gal. 1:11

- "I want you to know brothers, that. . ." ‒ Phil. 1:12 (close to #1)

Paul desired that the believers fully understand the main points of the gospel.

Church's questions (cf. 1 Cor. 7:1,25; 8:1; 12:1; also 1 Thess. 5:1).

▣ "we believe" This is the important theological VERB (PRESENT ACTIVE
INDICATIVE) for human's putting their faith in Christ. This is the Greek VERB
pisteuō, which is translated into English by "faith," "trust," or "believe."

This personal trust is characterized in the NT by using all the common Greek VERB TENSES:

- AORIST (past simple act), Acts 15:11; Rom. 8:24; 2 Tim.1:9; Titus 3:5

- PRESENT (ongoing process), 1 Cor. 1:18; 15:2; 2 Cor. 2:15; 1 Thess. 4:14

- PERFECT (past action which has come to completion and abides as a state
of being), Eph. 2:5,8

- FUTURE (in VERB TENSE or context), Rom. 5:9,10; 10:9;
13:11; 1 Cor. 3:15; Phil. 1:28; 1 Thess. 5:8-9; Heb. 1:14; 9:28

It is an initial decision, followed by lifestyle discipleship that will one day be
consummated in an eternal body and face-to-face fellowship with the Triune God (cf. 1 John 3:2). The
theological progression can be seen in Rom. 8:29-30, from election, to justification, to sanctification,
to glorification.

▣ "God will bring with Him" This is a difficult phrase because the VERB
(agō) has such a wide semantic field (to bring, to lead, to lead away, to lead out, to go, to go away,
etc.). Does it imply that

- the dead are with Jesus in heaven?

- the dead will be raised at Jesus' coming?

In context the PRONOUN refers to Jesus, at His second coming. The Thessalonian
believers did not understand Paul's preaching about the Second Coming. They wanted to know if those
of their church who had already died would participate in the end-time events. This is Paul's
positive response. Not only will they participate, they will receive their new bodies first and will
accompany Jesus on the clouds of heaven.

The NT is not clear about the state of believers between death and Resurrection Day. When
this passage is compared to 2 Cor. 5:6,8, postulating a disembodied period becomes a logical necessity (see Dale
Moody, The Word of Truth, pp. 499-502 and Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed.,
pp. 1179-1190). Believers are with the Lord, but as yet do not have their resurrection bodies.

The Bible does not give much information about the afterlife, probably because believers in their
fallen state could not comprehend its elements. A good small book that does discuss what the Bible reveals on
this issue is William Hendriksen, The Bible On the Life Hereafter.

This is the only place in the Bible the Rapture is revealed!

4:15 "For this we say to you by the word of the Lord" Paul was not giving his personal opinion but
was relating Jesus' teachings (cf. 1 Thess. 4:2; also note 1 Cor. 7:10), however, this particular saying of Jesus is
unrecorded in the Gospels. It is uncertain if this refers to

- oral Christian tradition (cf. Acts 20:35)

- Jesus' sermons, like Matt. 24 or Mark 13 or Luke 21

- if this was part of Jesus' personal revelation to Paul while in Arabia, Gal. 1:12; 2:2; Eph. 3:3

- later, direct revelation like 2 Cor. 12:1,9

This phrase implies that Paul is stating something he had received, which means that
his eschatological views were not uniquely his; he is passing on what he received. The problem is
we moderns do not know the source of this revelation or how widespread it was known.

We need to be reminded that the NT contains only a selected portion of Jesus' acts and
teachings (cf. John 20:30-31; 21:25). For a good brief discussion about this issue see Gordon Fee and Douglas
Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth, pp. 127-148; also note pp. 17-32.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELIC LEVELS IN PAUL'S WRITINGS

▣ "trumpet" The sounding of trumpets was a cultural way of announcing the approach of
royalty in the East (cf. Heb. 12:18-19). However, it also functions in other ways.

- divine judgment, Rev. 8:2; 11:15-19

- resurrection, 1 Cor. 15:52

- gathering of the elect by angels, Matt. 24:31

This was a very important means of communication in the OT, used for religious and
military events (cf. Exod. 19:16; Isa. 27:13; Joel 2:1; Zeph. 1:16; Zech. 9:14; 1 Cor. 15:52).

Two types of trumpets appear in the OT:

- silver trumpets (cf. Num. 10:2,8-10; 31:6)

- the left horn of a ram called the shophar (cf. Exod. 19:16,19; 20:18; Lev. 25:9; Joshua 6).

It is possible that all three sounds (shout, voice, trumpet) refer to the sounds made by the
angel because in Rev. 1:10; 4:1 the angel's voice is called a trumpet (cf. Rev. 1:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL

▣ "and the dead in Christ will rise first" This phrase causes confusion about where the
dead go between their death and resurrection day. This verse implies that they will remain in the
grave (cf. Matt. 27:52-53). However, 2 Cor. 5:6,8 implies that they are with the Lord. The solution
may be in postulating a disembodied state. The physical body remains in the grave, the life force goes
to be with the Lord. There are many unanswered questions here. The Bible does not provide a clear
teaching passage on this subject. See William Hendricksen, The Bible On the Life Hereafter.

Most translations translate it as if the saints are with God/Jesus and return with Him (cf. NASB).
Another view is found in TEV, "Those who have died believing in Christ will rise to life first."

4:17 "caught up" Our theological concept of "rapture" originates from this VERB. "Rapture"
is a Latin rendering of the Greek VERB here (harpazō - FUTURE
PASSIVE INDICATIVE), which implies a forceful "snatching away" (cf. John 6:15; 10:12, 28-29). 1 Cor. 15:51-52
also discusses Christians, alive and dead, receiving their new bodies (cf. 1 John 3:2).

Many godly, sincere, prayerful, educated believers have disagreed about this end-time event.
Some (i.e. particularly dispensationalists, but not me; see Dale Moody, The Word of Truth, pp. 555-557) expect a
secret rapture of believers (cf. Matt. 24:40-42) before a thousand-year reign of Christ
upon the earth. Often a seven year tribulation period (cf. Dan. 7:25; 9:27) is linked to this. Some theologians have the
rapture before, in the middle, or after a seven year tribulation period. The order and nature of these end-time events are ambiguous
at best. Dogmatism is surely inappropriate here. See my exegetical commentary on the book of Revelation online.

Believers are going to meet the Lord in the air, because in the NT the air was seen as
the realm of Satan (cf. Eph. 2:2) and Greeks thought the lower air (atmosphere) was unclean and,
therefore, the domain of unclean spirits. Believers will be reunited with their Lord in the midst
of Satan's kingdom to show its complete overthrow.

▣ "to meet" This is the Greek word apanēsis, which is used in the sense of
meeting someone and then accompanying them (cf. Matt. 25:6; Acts 28:15). So believers meet the Lord
in the air and return to a recreated earth with Him (this is my current understanding)!

▣ "in the air" The air was considered the dominion of Satan and his followers by first
century Judaism (cf. Eph. 2:2). We are going to meet the Lord there to show His complete victory. I
think that while believers are united with Christ in the air, the prophecy of the cleansing and renewal of
the earth in 2 Pet. 3:10 will occur. Heaven is depicted as a restored Garden of Eden (cf. Genesis 1-2
compared with Revelation 21-22).

▣ "we shall always be with the Lord" These Thessalonian believers will be united with their
dead believing loved ones by Jesus Himself. Nothing further can be said (cf. Psalm 23:6). The
Second Coming is referred to repeatedly in 1 Thessalonians (cf. 1 Thess. 1:10; 2:19; 3:13; 4:13-18; 5:1-11).
Notice that neither in this book nor 2 Thessalonians does Paul mention (some see 1 Cor. 15:25 as a
reference to an earthly reign) a thousand-year reign but an eternal reign, like Dan. 7:13-14.

Paul's terminology implies the eternal kingdom begins when Jesus returns. All of the
other end-time events are simply not mentioned as in 1 Cor. 15:50-58. Paul does not even imply that
Jesus returns completely to the earth. In Robert G. Clouses' The Meaning of the Millennium, all
four major millennial positions are articulated by various authors. In the a-millennial response
George E. Ladd makes this surprising statement, "I admit that the greatest difficulty to any
pre-millennialism is the fact that most of the New Testament pictures the consummation as occurring
at Jesus' parousia" (pp. 189-190). This is exactly what Paul is asserting here without any further elaboration.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Where in the Bible is the most detailed discussion of the Second Coming?

- What was the reason for Paul writing this passage?

- What is the Rapture? Who is involved? When will it occur?
